subject: Post-call recap — decision roles, procurement timeline & exception request (BlueStream POC)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluestreamhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <procurement@bluestreamhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — decision roles, procurement timeline & exception request (BlueStream POC)

Hi Alex + Priya,

Thanks again for the 30-minute sync this morning — good alignment on the technical fit and the POC success criteria. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of call:
- POC scope: 2 chatbot flows (triage + referral), ~15k tokens/day peak during trial.
- Success criteria: 90% intent-match on triage flow, <250ms median token latency for short-turn exchanges, and no egress of PHI to external logs.
- Decision roles you identified:
  - Alex Turner — Director of Eng (technical & infrastructure sign-off)
  - Priya Singh — Procurement (contract, timelines)
  - Lina Morales — Head of Product (product acceptance) — not on call but mentioned
  - CISO team (security questionnaire + endpoint isolation) — Priya to coordinate

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed):
1) Security & legal: I attached our standard security questionnaire and a draft SLA for review. Priya, can your CISO/IT team confirm whether the questionnaire requires a formal SOC2 report or if the completed questionnaire suffices for the POC?
2) Procurement timeline: you mentioned procurement is on a 4-week cadence but would prefer to accelerate for this POC. BlueStream asked if we can start on a 2-week onboarding with an internal exception for payment terms and a short-term 60-day invoice vs standard net-30. Priya, can you confirm whether that exception needs director-level approval?
3) Decision criteria & economic buyer: we heard Lina is the product owner but Alex noted the final economic signoff might be with Head of Ops (Samir). If possible, please confirm final economic approver so we can route paperwork correctly.
4) Demo & access: I'll send a calendar invite for an environment walkthrough next Wed (Jun 30).

Attachments: BlueStream_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, Redwood_POC_MAPlist.xlsx, Redwood_SLA-draft-v1.pdf

If this all looks right I can (a) submit an internal exception request for a 60-day invoice and a temporary SLA tweak for POC latency targets, and (b) provide a tight onboarding plan to meet a 2-week start.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0143
[attachment stub: Redwood_POC_MAPlist.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluestreamhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <procurement@bluestreamhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — decision roles, procurement timeline & exception request (BlueStream POC)

Thanks Camila — solid recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Security: Our CISO (cc: not on this thread yet) will want the SOC2 Type II report if it exists; otherwise, a completed questionnaire + the ability to host in our VPC will be required. I'll loop in Lina + Samir after I get confirmation from procurement.
- Procurement: Priya, we can try to move fast but need a signed buyer exception form signed by Samir (Head of Ops) for non-standard payment terms. If Redwood can commit to a short-term compliance attestation (no PHI egress, KMS key management options) that will help speed approval.
- Economic signoff: Likely Samir, yes. Lina will sign product acceptance after the POC.

Please proceed to submit whatever internal docs you need; we aim to decide on the exception within 7 business days if Redwood can provide the SOC2 or equivalent data points.

--
Alex Turner
Director of Engineering, BlueStream Health
alex.turner@bluestreamhealth.com
From: Priya Singh <procurement@bluestreamhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluestreamhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — decision roles, procurement timeline & exception request (BlueStream POC)

Camila — a few procurement notes: 

1) Exception path: non-standard payment terms (60-day invoice) require approval from Head of Ops (Samir) + Procurement Director (me). We can pre-approve the POC start pending the signed buyer-exception form and a short risk memo from your team.
2) Security artifacts: SOC2 report preferred. If you cannot provide SOC2, please fill the questionnaire fully and include answers for data residency, encryption in transit/at rest, and logging retention. Our security team will triage.
3) SLA: for POC we're flexible, but any change to SLA language around uptime or latency needs Legal + our CISO to sign off; Procurement can accept temporary addenda for the trial.

If you can get the buyer-exception form + completed questionnaire to me by Thurs (Jun 25), we can attempt the 2-week onboarding goal.

Regards,
Priya Singh
Procurement Director | BlueStream Health
procurement@bluestreamhealth.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bluestreamhealth.com>, Priya Singh <procurement@bluestreamhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — decision roles, procurement timeline & exception request (BlueStream POC)

Priyom / Neha — forwarding the thread above. BlueStream is receptive and asking us to: (1) provide SOC2 (preferred) or completed questionnaire, (2) submit buyer-exception form for 60-day invoice, and (3) sign a temporary SLA addendum for POC latency targets. They said they'll try to decide in ~7 business days if we deliver docs by Thu Jun 25.

Ask: I'd like to request an internal exception for the 60-day invoicing and a short-term SLA tweak for the POC (allowing our standard credit hold procedures to be delayed for 60 days and a POC-specific latency SLO). Proposed commercial concession: 10% trial discount applied for the 30-day POC in exchange for an accelerated start and a fast completion timeline.

Rationale: This is a strategic Coast-to-Coast health system with clear potential to expand to Dedicated capacity if the POC shows the cost/latency profile we promised. Speed to start is a competitive advantage here.

Can you advise on the internal approval path and who needs to sign the buyer-exception? Also need Legal involvement for the SLA addendum — Neha, can you please coordinate with Legal and R&D security to determine whether the questionnaire answers plus our KMS options will suffice in lieu of a SOC2? If we need to produce SOC2, we should surface that immediately (it will take time).

I attached a draft of the POC MAP and the SLA addendum. If you want, I can prepare a 1-page risk memo for the approvers and a structured pricing worksheet.

Thanks —
Camila
[attachment stub: Redwood_SLA-draft-v1.pdf (pdf)]
